title: VPA output to pitch plate -- the grip-length joint as a topology (L1 proof)

provenance.values: NONE are copied. Every edge carries a `dimension_ref` into the stack file above, resolved at load time by tolerance_stack.topology.load_topology, so this document cannot drift away from the numbers that stack publishes. Every value's citation and confidence is whatever that element already carries -- this topology adds no source_ref of its own to any value and closes no gap the stack has open.
provenance.structure: The nodes and the edge orientation are a READING of the stack's element order and roles, not a sourced claim. The stack transcribes workbook rows E63-E67 as an ordered clamped stack (bushing, spherical bearing, bushing flange, pitch flange, under-head washer) plus the fastener grip; laying those out head-side-first as six interfaces is this handoff's own arrangement. Two things make that safe to publish: a chain sum is invariant to the ordering (a signed term list does not care), and tests/test_topology.py pins the study's totals against the stack's own published check. What it is NOT is evidence that these specific faces mate in this order on the real part -- see notes.
provenance.part_identity: Four of the six parts are named on the stack's own citations (balloons 27, 28, 29 in 217755 sheet 5 DETAIL X, and the VPA assembly 208510-007 for the bearing). Two are not, and say so in their own `note` rather than borrowing a plausible drawing number.

parts.name: NAS6404U13D bolt, .2500-28, .812 grip
parts.note: Balloon 27, find 27 qty 1, in 217755 sheet 5 DETAIL X per the referenced stack element's source_ref. A standard part, so its dimensional identity is the NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet the element cites, not a Joby part drawing.

parts.name: MS21299C4K washer, countersunk, 17-4PH
parts.note: Balloon 29 in 217755 sheet 5 DETAIL X. The referenced element's nominal is sourced from the parts-list nomenclature; its BAND is not, and the element carries that as confidence `inferred` plus the repo's open gap.

parts.name: pitch flange (215197 A.1, feature ambiguous)
parts.note: Carried over from the referenced element, ambiguity included: 215197 prints TWO 4.06 +/-0.10 callouts and the element's own source_ref says the tolerance alone cannot decide between them, AND that DETAIL X balloons the TANGENTIAL LINK MOUNT 215175-002 rather than the pitch plate 215177-001, so 215197 may be the wrong part entirely. Named here as a part because the topology needs a lane for this thickness to be a dimension OF; the drawing number is the referenced element's claim, not a new one.

parts.name: the part carrying the bushing flange thickness -- NOT IDENTIFIED
parts.note: The referenced element `bushing_flange_thickness` cites workbook cell E65 and names no part at all. It is modelled as its own part because the flange is a separate 0.062 in feature from the straight bushing's length, and putting both dimensions on one part would be a structural claim (that they are one flanged bushing) with nothing behind it. Which part this is remains open -- see notes.

parts.name: spherical bearing, internal to 208510-007 VARIABLE PITCH ACTUATOR ASSEMBLY
parts.note: No balloon in DETAIL X: the referenced element's source_ref records it as internal to the VPA assembly (balloon 1). Its part number is not established -- the workbook's comment column names MS21299C4K on this row, and that part is the countersunk washer, not a bearing (the referenced stack's `column_I_caveat`).

parts.name: BUSHING, PLAIN, ALUMINUM BRONZE, .250 in ID (Joby 214943-002)
parts.note: Balloon 28 in DETAIL X, per the referenced element's source_ref. That element's modelled length is still `untraced` and still on the gap list: NAS77A4-015, the number the source workbook names, was RULED OUT on the merits in 2026-08-13 and 214943-002's own part drawing is not in the pile.

nodes.name: bolt-head bearing face against the countersunk washer
nodes.note: Where the grip is measured from: NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet 2 note (a) defines grip as underside of head to the end of the full cylindrical shank, per the referenced fastener element's source_ref.

nodes.name: washer face against the pitch flange
pitch flange face against the bushing flange
bushing flange face against the spherical bearing
spherical bearing face against the plain bushing
plain bushing far face -- the last clamped surface
nodes.note: A datum_feature and not a mating_surface: what is beyond it is the castellated nut's face, and the nut is deliberately outside this joint's scope (see notes).

nodes.name: end of the bolt's full cylindrical shank
nodes.note: The grip's far end, defined by NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet 2 note (a). Not a mate: it is where the thread run-out begins.

edges.name: fastener grip (.812 in)
edges.note: The one edge that runs PARALLEL to the clamped stack rather than in series with it. Together with `shank_out` it closes the loop, and that loop closure is what the stack's `worst_case_shank_out` check computes.

edges.name: shank out -- full-diameter shank beyond the clamped stack
edges.note: A DERIVED gap: it carries no dimension because it is the quantity a study computes, not one that is measured. Study `vpa_output_shank_out` names it in `closes`. Negative at the minimum means the thread run-out is pulled inside the joint; positive at the maximum means full-diameter shank protrudes past the nut face -- the referenced stack's own guidance.

notes: This document is the L1 proof of the topology format: an existing, reviewed, committed grip stack re-expressed as a graph, with the summation checked to the digit against what that stack already publishes. It adds no value, no citation and no confidence claim of its own. If a number here looks wrong, the stack file is where it is wrong.

The topology holds one loop -- the fastener in parallel with the clamped stack it passes through -- and NO branch point (no node has three edges). That is what makes it L1: the traversal never has to choose. The pitch-system topology is where branching starts.

The as-drawn joint is retained by a castellated nut (MS9363-10, balloon 25) and a cotter pin (MS24665-229, balloon 26), and the referenced stack states plainly that grip length alone cannot answer this joint: the binding constraint is whether a castellation slot lines up with the cotter hole. Neither the stack nor this topology models that. `bushing_far_face` is therefore a datum_feature rather than a mate -- the nut is not in this graph.

OPEN, for Jeff: is `bushing_flange_thickness` the flange of the SAME part as `straight_bushing` (one flanged bushing) or a separate part? Modelled here as two parts because the referenced element names no part for the flange, and merging them would be a structural claim with no source. It changes no total either way -- a structural dimension and a gap fold identically -- but it changes the swim-lane rendering and it changes what a 3D-annotation surface would have to resolve.

OPEN, for Jeff: this topology asserts an axial ORDER for the clamped members (washer, pitch flange, bushing flange, bearing, bushing, head-side first) taken from the source workbook's row order. The sum does not depend on it; a reader looking at the rail diagram will nonetheless read it as physical. Worth one look at DETAIL X to confirm or correct before the viewer renders it.
